section: Base units H. 84 | for household appliances
source_pages: printed p.55-56 / PDF 57-58 (subset: the two dishwasher-door series of p.55)
extraction_note: 2026-09-28, the 7612 perimeter moves to H.84 (Andriy). HELD: the two dishwasher-door series of printed p.55 and nothing else on p.55-56, by Andriy's decision the same day - the plain tall door VL0640 / VL0740 (buildable; filler profile and GBBF01 as companions) and the two-front door VL8659 (held, not buildable - see its reason). REMOVED the same day, by decision and not by oversight: the platform door VL0630 / VL0730, the fridge housing VL0601 / VN0601 and the washing-machine door VL0650. NOT CODES HERE, BUT ON THE PAGE: 'Protection under induction hob (custom sizing not available)' 996466 (60), 996467 (75), 996469 (90), 996460 (105), 996462 (120), priced in points - an accessory ordered with a hob, not a companion of any base. For 7612, BM0967 under the CIT36YWBB takes 996469 as a manual order line. THE HOUSING FITS: Thermador DWHD660EPR is 860-890 mm high, adjustable (Vol. 10.1 p.223), and the H.84 housing is 870 floor to gola recess or 900 floor to the worktop underside. What the same drawing also dimensions is the PANEL: its lower edge 700-765 mm below the countertop's bottom edge, over a toe kick of 92-190. The H.84 door runs to the 60 plinth line (840 / 810), so its lower edge sits lower than that drawing allows - recorded, the choice is Andriy's.
representation_notes: THE PLINTH UNDER A DISHWASHER PANEL IS DRAWN, AND THE ONE ORDERED IS A DIFFERENT ARTICLE. UCON decision, Andriy, 2026-08-24, off the Avenida Primavera kitchen. Until today this registry said a dishwasher panel gets no plinth, and about the JOINERY that was correct: the plinth in front of the machine is cut away or the door cannot fall. About the DRAWING it was wrong - the plinth line then breaks on the LayOut elevation exactly where a machine stands, and the sheet reads as a hole. So the panel now carries a plinth box and its phantom housing starts on top of it, the same treatment the US fridge housing already had. BOTH ARE REPRESENTATION. What the warehouse must be asked for is a plinth WITH A CUTOUT. Andriy: designers routinely order plain linear plinth instead and the cutout gets improvised on site at installation - which is the reason to hold the two facts apart in writing rather than let a drawing imply an order. The order side is deliberately deferred and not written yet.

AND THE 'cutout for plinth 40' PRINTED ON printed p.47 AND p.48 IS STILL UNREAD. It now has a plausible home - 40 mm taken out of the plinth in front of the machine - but plausible is not printed, and domain rule 1 says the source wins. Left open on purpose (Andriy, 2026-08-24: not urgent). Nothing in the geometry depends on it: the drawn plinth is full height, and the cutout, whatever it turns out to be, belongs to the order line.

appliance_dishwasher_door.description: Tall door for dishwasher - 1 door, profile with infill front on request, without fixing holes

appliance_niche.note: DRAWN, NOT MEASURED - see representation_notes at the head of this file. No top_mm: the housing ends where the panel ends and the generator already knows that number.

front_layout.note: One full-height panel hinged along its bottom edge, carried by the machine. Per docs/Drawing_Spec_v0.1.md the elevation symbol is the inverted V and the plan shows it fallen forward by the front height. Not rendered yet - 70_symbols draws a single leaf only when a hinge_side is given, and this object never has one, so nothing is drawn rather than something wrong.

companions.note: Filler profile between the dishwasher and the top: 995945 (45) and 995946 (60) printed on p.56. H.84 has no 45 cm dishwasher door, so only 995946 is used; the 75 cm door takes it because the machine behind it is 60 wide.
Stainless steel cabinet W150 with the door-bearing mechanism, for the 75 cm version only (60 + 15). No depth printed and its side is Elda Q5 - order line, not geometry, as at H.78.

appliance_dishwasher_door.notes: TWIN OF appliance_h78 / appliance_dishwasher_door: same position, same wording, same shape on the H.84 page; keys carried from it, codes, elevation and glyphs re-read on the H.84 page itself. Printed 'Tall door for dishwasher' at H.84 - one door, profile with infill front on request, without fixing holes. W60 and W75 only (no 45 at H.84). Elevation 84 / 81. The 75 cm version: 'a stainless steel cabinet is installed adjacent to the 60 cm wide appliance. An automatic opening and closing mechanism is installed on the right-hand side panel.' No hung glyph and no margin surcharges beside this position.

appliance_dishwasher_door_aluminium_prof.not_buildable_reason: TWO FRONTS THAT DO NOT SUM TO THE FAMILY GOLA DOOR. Elevation printed p.55: 33 / 45 = 780, where the H.84 gola door is 810. 810 minus one 30 recess is 780, so the pair reads as a gola panel with one groove between the fronts - our reading, as at H.78, and the same family-scoped door_versions blocker. Held, findable, orderable, not drawn.
